subject: Post-call: FintechCo integration + observability hooks
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: dylan.brooks@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: integration & observability hooks

Hi Alex — great to meet today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our call so we keep momentum: 

Summary of needs
- SDK setup + auth: FintechCo will host instances in us-west; prefers service account / OIDC for server-side calls.
- Routing & structured outputs: need deterministic routing for low-latency flows and structured tool-calling for payments workflows.
- Embeddings & reranker: evaluate semantic search for transaction enrichment; expect ~50k docs, embeddings at 1536 dim.
- Observability: require trace propagation, per-request latency breakdowns, and logs with model/route context for billing reconciliation.

Deliverables I said we'd share
1) Redwood observability integration guide (attached) — includes recommended headers, sample logs, and tracing examples.
2) Short mutual action plan with milestones and owners (attached).
3) Proposed tech-deep dive with our SEs (can do Thu or Fri next week).

Immediate asks for you
- Confirm whether you want API keys or OIDC service accounts for initial PoC.
- Share a sample request/response schema for the structured outputs you expect (tool-calling payloads).

I pasted a short excerpt from the guide below on recommended headers/log fields for quick reference. Full docs attached.

Recommended headers & logging fields (excerpt)
- Headers: X-Request-ID (incoming), X-Redwood-Trace-ID (propagated), X-Fintech-User-ID
- Latency headers (returned by Redwood): X-Redwood-Latency-Total-ms, X-Redwood-Latency-Inference-ms, X-Redwood-Latency-Network-ms
- Logging fields to include in your traces/logs: redwood.request_id, redwood.model, redwood.route, redwood.latency.total_ms, redwood.latency.inference_ms, redwood.latency.network_ms
- Recommended trace sampling: 1% full-span capture, 100% short-span with metadata

Next step: can you confirm auth preference and whether Thu 3/12 10am PT works for a tech deep dive?

Thanks,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — useful recap. A few clarifying items from our side: 

1) Auth: we prefer OIDC service accounts for server-to-server calls. Can you share a short runbook for configuring OIDC with Redwood? Specifically: token lifetime, rotation, and any required claims.

2) Trace IDs: would X-Redwood-Trace-ID be sufficient for joining traces across systems, or do you have span IDs we should propagate? We want to ensure our observability team can stitch Redwoods' traces into our Jaeger setup.

3) Latency breakdowns: we need to show a per-request breakdown in our dashboard (network vs inference). Is the X-Redwood-Latency-* header returned on every request, or only for sampled traces?

4) Embeddings: sounds like 50k docs. Curious about throughput and batching recommendations for indexing (we use k8s, 8 nodes). Any best-practice for retries/errors?

Thurs 3/12 10am PT works for the tech deep dive. I can loop in our lead engineer (cc'd devops@).

Appreciate it — Alex

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>
Cc: dylan.brooks@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: integration & observability hooks

Alex — thanks and great questions. Quick answers below and Dylan will add a few engineering specifics ahead of the call.

1) OIDC runbook: attached in the guide (section 2). Short answers: recommended token lifetime 15m for access tokens + 1h refresh window; we support rotating JWKS and token introspection. We can also issue short-lived API keys for testing but for PoC we recommend OIDC service accounts.

2) Trace propagation: X-Redwood-Trace-ID is the canonical request-level id we accept and return. For span-level details we expose an optional header X-Redwood-Span-Ids that contains a comma-separated list of span ids when full-span capture is enabled (sampling). To stitch with Jaeger, send X-Redwood-Trace-ID and include opentracing-compatible spans; we can provide a small adapter snippet in the guide.

3) Latency headers: X-Redwood-Latency-* are returned on every response but with numeric values only when sampling is enabled for detailed spans. We always return X-Redwood-Latency-Total-ms for bookkeeping; inference/network breakdowns are populated when trace capture is on (sampling). We'll include a lightweight header variant for aggregated dashboards if you need per-request breakdown without full-span capture.

4) Embeddings indexing: for ~50k docs we recommend batch size 256-512 depending on your pod memory and concurrency. Use the bulk embeddings endpoint with exponential backoff for 429/5xx. We include idempotency keys for safe retries. We'll include code samples in the guide (Python/Go).

I'll also attach the mutual action plan with owners and Milestone: PoC (API + basic observability) -> Pilot (reranker + dashboards) -> Prod rollout.

Looking forward to the call Thu 3/12 10am PT. Dylan, can you prepare a 20-minute architecture mini-deck (auth flow, header propagation, sample logs) and a short snippet for Jaeger/OTel integration?

Best,
Marissa

Hey Alex — Dylan from Redwood infra/SE team here. Short technical notes ahead of the deep dive and a couple of code snippets to get you unblocked.

Auth (OIDC)
- We support OIDC token exchange (RFC 8693). Configure your service account to get short-lived access tokens (15m). Redwood validates iss/aud and jwks. Sample claim required: sub, aud, exp.
- If you want automatic rotation, we support supplying our token endpoint with your JWKS and we can rotate keys on our end.

Headers & trace propagation (recommended flow)
- Incoming request from your app -> attach X-Request-ID and X-Fintech-User-ID
- Set X-Redwood-Trace-ID: uuidv4 per request (your proxy or app can generate)
- Redwood will return: X-Redwood-Trace-ID (echo), X-Redwood-Latency-Total-ms, and when sampled: X-Redwood-Latency-Inference-ms, X-Redwood-Latency-Network-ms, X-Redwood-Span-Ids

Example curl (embedding call)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <OIDC-token>" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Trace-ID: 123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"documents": ["..."], "batch_size": 256, "idempotency_key": "bulk-20260310-1"}'

Sample log fields (structured JSON)
{
  "ts": "2026-03-12T16:00:00Z",
  "level": "info",
  "redwood.request_id": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000",
  "redwood.trace_id": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000",
  "redwood.model": "open-llm-1.2-q8",
  "redwood.route": "low-latency-payments",
  "redwood.latency.total_ms": 123,
  "redwood.latency.inference_ms": 95,
  "redwood.latency.network_ms": 18
}

Observability integration notes
- For dashboards: use X-Redwood-Latency-Total-ms as a per-request metric. For split inference vs network, enable 1% sampling and push full spans to your Jaeger/OTel collector.
- We recommend storing redwood.trace_id in your logs at ingestion time so you can join traces and logs in your SIEM.
- If you need billing reconciliation, include redwood.route and model in your log ingestion.

Next steps (short)
- Tech deep dive Thu 3/12 10am PT (confirmed)
- I will share a 6-slide deck + OIDC snippet to the Drive link before the call.
- Marissa to share PoC MSA + scope for procurement.

Looking forward — Dylan
